title: The Wrong Portrait
premise: Felix Joubert takes a teaching post in a fog-bound coastal village where students vanish one by one, always the ones no one seems to remember well. His rented cottage belonged to the Joubert family he never knew he had, and its mirrors begin showing the rooms a heartbeat behind reality—then showing people who aren't there. The disappearances are a harvest: the village's founding families feed their forgotten kin to the house before the harvest moon, and Felix's arrival completes the count. To save his remaining students and the last of the family, Felix must burn his own documentation—the prayer that has been binding them to the house—and lead everyone out across the salt marsh before the moon rises, ending with the mirrors reflecting only what is truly there, and Felix finally choosing to be remembered.
about_author: Marguerite Quintana is a former rural schoolteacher who writes horror rooted in coastal folklore and the quiet dread of institutional buildings after dark. She lives near the sea, keeps no mirrors in her writing room, and insists her family tree has a gap no archivist can explain.

chapters.title: The Attendance Sheet
chapters.summary: Felix arrives in the village of Sainte-Brume to teach at a school with too few students and too many empty desks. He begins his ritual of documenting everything in a leather ledger, a habit born of a childhood spent unseen. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: cautious hope masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Names
chapters.summary: The school register lists twenty-six students, but Felix can count only nineteen in class, and the headmaster, Madame Oury, deflects questions with bureaucratic smiles. A student, Solène, whispers that the missing ones 'went home' though they lived in the village. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: first crack of unease.

chapters.title: The House That Waited
chapters.summary: Felix moves into a cheap cottage on Rue du Sel and finds it oddly prepared: beds made, a child's drawings in a drawer, a family Bible with the surname Joubert. He tells himself it's coincidence. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: uncanny belonging he doesn't want.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: At 3:07 a.m., Felix notices the bathroom mirror shows him lifting his hand a beat after he does. He tests it with matches, coins, his ledger—always one second late. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: vertigo; the documented world stops matching the document.

chapters.title: Solène Counts the Chairs
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Solène, twelve, who keeps her own secret tally of vanished classmates scratched into her pencil case. She watches Felix, testing whether he'll forget her too. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two people who refuse to forget.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Almanac
chapters.summary: In the cottage attic Felix finds an almanac marking every harvest moon for two centuries, each with a number beside it—numbers that match the missing students. The last page lists this year's moon and a final count. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: The mirrors begin showing the room as it was decades ago: a woman braiding a child's hair, a boy at a desk. Felix recognizes his own face in the boy. The house isn't haunted; it's remembering him. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: inheritance as horror.

chapters.title: Madame Oury's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Oury, who reveals the school's true function: the founding families 'tithe' their least-remembered relatives to the house each generation, keeping the village prosperous. She offers Felix a choice—join the count or be counted. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the institution as predator.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Went Home
chapters.summary: Solène leads Felix to the salt marsh where the missing students appear at dusk, translucent, mouthing their own names as if rehearsing them. They can't cross the treeline. POV: Solène. Emotional beat: grief for the half-erased.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Felix realizes his ledger's meticulous records have been anchoring the students' fading identities—and that the house has been reading his pages at night, learning the names faster than he can write them. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: his coping ritual is the trap.

chapters.title: Aunt Marguerite
chapters.summary: The mirror-woman—Felix's great-aunt, erased from every record in 1943—speaks through the glass, explaining the family bargain and warning that the house needs a Joubert to complete this year's count. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: kinship with a ghost, terror of the role he's inherited.

chapters.title: Roll Call at Midnight
chapters.summary: The school holds a midnight 'makeup session' for the missing students; Felix attends hidden and watches the founding families lead children into the boiler-room cellar, where the walls drink their reflections first. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: horror of complicit community.

chapters.title: Solène's Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix finds Solène's name freshly inked on the harvest page—Oury has added her. With six days to the moon, he decides to stop documenting and start destroying. POV: Solène. Emotional beat: fear becoming defiance.

chapters.title: Burning the Prayer
chapters.summary: Felix burns his ledger page by page in the cottage hearth; each flame frees a memory—the mirrors flicker, the translucent students gain color. But the house retaliates, sealing doors and flooding rooms with remembered pasts. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: With the ledger burned, the villagers begin forgetting their own bargains; Oury grows desperate and hunts Felix through streets that keep rearranging into older versions of themselves. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: The Count Is Wrong
chapters.summary: Oury corners Felix at the school: the count needs one more, and she'll take him at the moonrise. Solène and three remaining students rescue him using the translucent ones' knowledge of the house's blind spots. POV: Solène. Emotional beat: solidarity against the harvest.

chapters.title: What Aunt Marguerite Left Behind
chapters.summary: The great-aunt's mirror-message reveals the escape route: the founding families' own forgotten dead walk a path through the marsh that the house cannot watch, open only while the moon is still below the horizon. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: inheritance repurposed as salvation.

chapters.title: Moonrise Preparations
chapters.summary: The village readies its harvest feast; the founding families dress their chosen children in white. Felix and Solène gather every student who still has a name and plan the crossing for the hour before moonrise. POV: alternating Felix and Solène. Emotional beat: quiet, terrified resolve.

chapters.title: The Hour Before the Moon
chapters.summary: The escape begins: children led across the marsh by the translucent dead, the house screaming through every mirror in the village, Oury and the families in pursuit with lanterns. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: flight, sacrifice, the dead buying time.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: At the marsh's heart the path narrows; Oury catches Solène, and Felix trades himself for her, stepping into the house's grasp as the moon crests. But his burned ledger left him with no reflection to take—the count fails, and the house begins to starve. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax; self-erasure inverted into weapon.

chapters.title: After the Harvest
chapters.summary: The house collapses inward, releasing two centuries of taken names; the translucent students wake solid and weeping on the marsh grass. Oury and the founders, their bargain void, age into their own forgotten years. POV: Solène. Emotional beat: grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: The New Register
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Felix teaches a full classroom and starts a new ledger—this time recording names so they're shared, not hoarded. The cottage mirrors show only the present, and in one of them, briefly, Aunt Marguerite smiles and is gone. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, memory as gift.
